anchor.quote: The integer $s$ is the number of coordinates of a source vector.
The integer $t$ is the number of coordinates of a target vector
The integer $\alpha\ge 2$ sets the width of the Gaussian weights.
$F_s$ is the normalized Fourier transform of length $s$
$P_s$ is the permutation $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ of length-$s$ vectors
$P_t$ is the permutation $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ of length-$t$ vectors

anchor.note: The page never says what v denotes; it only says P_t acts on length-t vectors, so v is presumably a length-t vector, but this is not stated. The earlier binding of v (second integer, radix-digit-convolution) is a different meaning.

anchor.quote: $A$ is a linear contraction from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors.
$B_0$ is a linear contraction from length-$t$ to length-$s$ vectors.
The proof uses two Gaussian-weighted maps $S$ and $T$ from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors
The proof uses two Gaussian-weighted maps $S$ and $T$ from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors
$q_j$ is the integer nearest $tj/s$, with ties rounded upward.
The map $C$ selects the coordinates $q_0,\dots,q_{s-1}$ from a length-$t$ vector.
The map $D$ is the diagonal map
The operator $N=CTD$ is near the identity.

anchor.note: Identity matrix/map, from the linear algebra course (matrices, invertibility); the page uses it in ||N-I|| without saying what it denotes.
The constant pi, covered by the basics of complex numbers and roots of unity.
The base of the exponential, covered by the basics of complex numbers (e^{i theta}).
The integers, covered by the discrete mathematics and radix representation of integers.

gaps.quote: A linear contraction is a linear map of norm at most one.
gaps.note: The norm of a linear map (operator norm) is not among the reader's known concepts and the page neither explains it nor links it. Contraction, S', J', D', C and N all depend on it.
The identity is asserted with no proof, no citation, and no statement that it is the Gaussian resampling identity. The reader cannot check it from the page, and the whole argument depends on it.

gaps.quote: Its $j$-th output is $u_j$ plus a small error, so $\|N-I\|<1/2$.
gaps.note: The page gives no estimate of the error term in N u, so the reader cannot check that the operator norm of N - I is below 1/2.
The Neumann series is named but neither explained nor linked. The reader does not know that the series converges when the norm of I - N is below one, or that its sum inverts N.

gaps.term: norm bounds on S', J', D'
gaps.note: The page gives no computation for these bounds. They would need bounds on the norms of S, N^{-1} and D (for example, from the size of the Gaussian weights and the entries of D), none of which the page states.
The page does not say why the indices q_j are distinct (which is what makes C a coordinate selection of norm one), nor how the norm of a selection map is computed. The reader cannot check ||C|| = 1.
